verses.pali: Saṁyutta Nikāya 35.124
verses.english: Linked Discourses 35.124

verses.pali: 13. Gahapativagga
verses.english: 13. Householders

verses.pali: Vesālīsutta
verses.english: At Vesālī

verses.pali: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā vesāliyaṁ viharati mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṁ.
verses.english: At one time the Buddha was staying near Vesālī, at the Great Wood, in the hall with the peaked roof.

verses.pali: Atha kho uggo gahapati vesāliko yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho uggo gahapati vesāliko bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: Then the householder Ugga of Vesālī went up to the Buddha, sat down to one side, and said to him:

verses.pali: “ko nu kho, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo yena m’idhekacce sattā diṭṭheva dhamme no parinibbāyanti?
verses.english: “What is the cause, sir, what is the reason why some sentient beings are not fully extinguished in this very life?

verses.pali: Ko pana, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo yena m’idhekacce sattā diṭṭheva dhamme parinibbāyantī”ti?
verses.english: What is the cause, sir, what is the reason why some sentient beings are fully extinguished in this very life?”

verses.pali: “Santi kho, gahapati, cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā.
verses.english: “Householder, there are sights known by the eye, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

verses.pali: Tañce bhikkhu abhinandati abhivadati ajjhosāya tiṭṭhati. Tassa taṁ abhinandato abhivadato ajjhosāya tiṭṭhato tannissitaṁ viññāṇaṁ hoti tadupādānaṁ.
verses.english: If a mendicant approves, welcomes, and keeps clinging to them, their consciousness has that as support and fuel for grasping.

verses.pali: Saupādāno, gahapati, bhikkhu no parinibbāyati …pe…
verses.english: A mendicant with fuel for grasping does not become extinguished.

verses.pali: santi kho, gahapati, jivhāviññeyyā rasā …pe…
verses.english: There are sounds … smells … tastes … touches …

verses.pali: santi kho, gahapati, manoviññeyyā dhammā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā.
verses.english: ideas known by the mind, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

verses.pali: Tañce bhikkhu abhinandati abhivadati ajjhosāya tiṭṭhati. Tassa taṁ abhinandato abhivadato ajjhosāya tiṭṭhato tannissitaṁ viññāṇaṁ hoti tadupādānaṁ.
verses.english: If a mendicant approves, welcomes, and keeps clinging to them, their consciousness has that as support and fuel for grasping.

verses.pali: Saupādāno, gahapati, bhikkhu no parinibbāyati.
verses.english: A mendicant with fuel for grasping does not become extinguished.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ kho, gahapati, hetu, ayaṁ paccayo yena m’idhekacce sattā diṭṭheva dhamme no parinibbāyanti.
verses.english: That’s the cause, that’s the reason why some sentient beings are not fully extinguished in this very life.

verses.pali: Santi ca kho, gahapati, cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā, iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā.
verses.english: There are sights known by the eye, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

verses.pali: Tañce bhikkhu nābhinandati nābhivadati nājjhosāya tiṭṭhati. Tassa taṁ anabhinandato anabhivadato anajjhosāya tiṭṭhato na tannissitaṁ viññāṇaṁ hoti, na tadupādānaṁ.
verses.english: If a mendicant doesn’t approve, welcome, and keep clinging to them, their consciousness doesn’t have that as support and fuel for grasping.

verses.pali: Anupādāno, gahapati, bhikkhu parinibbāyati …pe…
verses.english: A mendicant free of grasping becomes extinguished.

verses.pali: santi kho, gahapati, jivhāviññeyyā rasā …pe…
verses.english: There are sounds … smells … tastes … touches …

verses.pali: santi kho, gahapati, manoviññeyyā dhammā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā.
verses.english: ideas known by the mind, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

verses.pali: Tañce bhikkhu nābhinandati nābhivadati nājjhosāya tiṭṭhati, tassa taṁ anabhinandato anabhivadato anajjhosāya tiṭṭhato. Na tannissitaṁ viññāṇaṁ hoti, na tadupādānaṁ.
verses.english: If a mendicant doesn’t approve, welcome, and keep clinging to them, their consciousness doesn’t have that as support and fuel for grasping.

verses.pali: Anupādāno, gahapati, bhikkhu parinibbāyati.
verses.english: A mendicant free of grasping becomes extinguished.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ kho, gahapati, hetu ayaṁ paccayo yena m’idhekacce sattā diṭṭheva dhamme parinibbāyantī”ti.
verses.english: That’s the cause, that’s the reason why some sentient beings are fully extinguished in this very life.”

verses.pali: Paṭhamaṁ.
